business_problem: Worley needed to unlock more than 50 years of engineering knowledge across over 100,000 documents, but fragmented tools, isolated repositories, and slow document retrieval caused engineers to waste time and made it hard to get accurate answers quickly.
solution_summary: Worley built Worley AI.Assist as a unified engineering knowledge assistant on NVIDIA's enterprise AI stack. NVIDIA NIM microservices provide the layer for deploying and managing multiple LLMs and embedding models across Worley's global infrastructure, while NVIDIA Triton Inference Server lets the assistant serve several model types simultaneously with lower latency. For retrieval, NVIDIA NeMo Retriever converts both queries and source documents into vector embeddings so the system can find the most relevant engineering information, and a GPU-accelerated Milvus vector database performs similarity search across 100,000-plus document embeddings. Above that stack, Worley supports conversational search, uploaded-document question answering, temporary document snapshots, and agentic routing to specialized analysis tools, with results for some workflows stored in Microsoft Azure. Together, these layers turn a fragmented engineering corpus into a governed, scalable virtual assistant.

data_flow: User questions or uploaded engineering files enter Worley AI.Assist, NeMo Retriever embeds both queries and documents, Milvus returns relevant knowledge-base matches, Triton and NIM serve the language and embedding models, and specialized document-analysis workflows can route results into Azure while the assistant returns cited answers to engineers.
business_outcome: Worley cut document-delivery and reading tasks from more than 15 minutes to under 5 minutes, is scaling toward 50,000 employees and 100,000-plus documents with 350 concurrent users, and targets 99.99 percent uptime for a secure knowledge platform that improves engineering productivity.
metrics: From 15+ minutes to less than 5 minutes
